# 04 Handle all four action kinds in next(), add prev()

## Outcome

`createAnimationController`'s `next()` applies the correct class mutation for whichever action
kind(s) are assigned to the newly-current step (`enter`, `exit`, `highlight`, `unhighlight`).
`prev()` is a new method that moves `currentStep` back by one and applies the canonical DOM class
state for that step's cumulative history — instantly, no transition.

## Implementation guidance (not a hard requirement, but the recommended approach)

Scope `transition` CSS declarations to the effect classes themselves
(`siren-enter-*`/`siren-exit-*`/`siren-highlight-*`), never to a persistent base rule — that's
ticket 06's concern (the shipped stylesheet), but it's *why* this ticket doesn't need any special
"disable transitions" mechanism: compute the canonical class set for the target step and apply it
directly (add missing classes, remove extra ones). Removing a class that carried the only relevant
`transition` declaration reverts the property instantly, for free, in a real browser. Do not
implement `prev()` by replaying `next()`'s per-call diffs in reverse — compute the target step's
state directly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Given a fixture with `enter B fade` (step 1), `highlight B outline` (step 1, same step as
  its own enter), `exit A fade` (step 2), `highlight A-B glow` (step 2), `unhighlight A-B`
  (step 3): calling `next()` three times applies, at each step, exactly the class mutations
  implied by that step's actions — `siren-pending` → `siren-enter-fade` for B; `siren-highlight-outline`
  added to B; `siren-exit-fade` added to A (staying in the DOM); `siren-highlight-glow` added to
  the `A-B` edge; then `siren-highlight-glow` removed from `A-B` on the third `next()`.
- [ ] A second `highlight` action on the same element with a different effect (e.g. `outline` at
  step 1, `glow` at step 3) results in only `siren-highlight-glow` present after both have fired —
  the old effect class is removed when the new one is added, never stacked.
- [ ] Calling `prev()` after N `next()` calls produces, for every element, the same class list as
  would result from N-1 `next()` calls from a fresh controller — verified against a fixture
  exercising all four action kinds across at least 3 steps.
- [ ] `prev()` at `currentStep === 0` is a no-op — no error, `currentStep` stays 0.
- [ ] `reset()` still restores the initial state (unchanged from the first slice) — every element
  with an `enter` action back to `siren-pending`, no `siren-highlight-*`/`siren-exit-*` classes
  present, `currentStep === 0`.
